paragraphs: Here's what I love about Caleb, friend. He didn't ask for the easy land. He asked for the hill country, where the Anakim lived in great and fortified cities, and he asked at eighty-five years old. Why? Because the LORD had promised it, and Caleb believed that promise the whole time (Joshua 14:12).

The passage says it twice: Caleb "wholly followed the LORD" (Joshua 14:9, 14). That's the heart of it. For forty-five years Caleb didn't wait around with his arms crossed. He kept walking with God, and the LORD kept him alive and strong the whole way (Joshua 14:10-11). Notice how Caleb talks, too. He doesn't say "I'll crush them." He says, "Perhaps with the LORD's help I will drive them out" (Joshua 14:12). His strength was real, but his hope sat in the LORD.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Following God all the way is a long game, and a promise from Him is worth holding onto even when the wait feels longer than a Monday. Caleb's story says the LORD notices faithfulness, and Joshua blessed him and gave him Hebron (Joshua 14:13). You don't have to be the loudest or the youngest. Just keep following Him wholly, and let Him handle the giants.
